messages.content: what is the difference between put the book away and put off reading the book?
put the book away usually is about moving it to the place where you keep it. put off reading the book is about choosing to read later, rather than now.
make that explanation shorter.
put the book away is about where you put it. put off reading the book is about choosing to read later.
can i put it away and still read it today?
yes. you could put it on the shelf now and take it out to read this evening.
can i put off reading while leaving it on the table?
yes. you can leave the book where it is and choose to read later. moving the book and changing your reading time are different things.
now give me one sentence with both ideas.
i put the book away and chose to read it later.
use put off in that sentence too.
i put the book away and put off reading it until later.
does that say i never read it?
no. it says you chose a later time. it does not tell us whether you really read it then.
only give the sentence about the shelf.
i put the book on the shelf.
if i say not everyone came, does that mean nobody came?
no. it says the whole group did not all come. some people may have come, but the sentence does not give the number.
can you give a short example?
if four people were coming and only three came, you could say not everyone came.
there were four friends, and three came. can i say not everyone came?
yes. one of the four did not come, so not everyone came is true.
can i say nobody came?
no. three came, so nobody came would be false.
what if no friends came at all?
then nobody came is true. not everyone came can also be true, but nobody came gives the information more clearly.
now say only what happened with three out of four.
three of the four friends came. one did not come.
can you know why the one did not come?
no. you have not said which friend did not come or why.
only say what you do not know.
i do not know which friend did not come or why.
write a story about a person who can read small words but wants the page in front of him. do not say he cannot read at all.

a grandfather sat at the table while his daughter held a page across from him. she asked whether he could read the first sentence. he said he could read the words, but wanted the page in front of him. she moved her chair and put the paper where he wanted it. he read the sentence and asked about a word he had not used before. they talked about it, then read the next line together. his request to move the page had not said that he understood nothing. it was a request for a simple change that helped him use what he already knew.
what did he ask for first?
he asked for the page to be put in front of him.
did that tell his daughter he could not read any words?
no. he said he could read the words. the page place was the first problem.
why did he ask about one word after reading?
he had not used that word before. knowing how to read a sentence does not always mean knowing every word in it.
write that as a question from the grandfather.
could you put the page in front of me, please?
can you finish with him helping his daughter too?
after they read the page, he told her about an old story that used the new word in a different way. she listened and wrote down the example.
what helped each person learn something?
they each had something to learn and something to share.
i sat inside while the rain came down. i want to write a sentence about it, but do not say i was sad or happy.
i sat inside while the rain came down.
i was looking out of the window. add that.
then write: i sat inside and looked at the rain through the window.
can you make it a little longer without making up a feeling?
i sat inside and looked through the window while the rain came down outside.
now add that i was at the table.
i sat at the table and looked through the window at the rain.
why are those small place details important?
because you want a sentence about what really happened. sitting by a window and seeing it from a table can give a different picture of the room.
now i want a made up story instead. can you add a feeling then?
yes, if we keep it clear that it is a story. tell me what feeling you want, or i can choose one for the person in the story.
use calm, and make the person not me.
a woman sat at the table, looking through the window at the rain. she felt calm as the room grew quiet.
only give my real sentence again.
i sat at the table and looked through the window at the rain.
there are five chairs in the kitchen and two in the bedroom. i move two from the kitchen to the bedroom. how many are in each room?
there are three in the kitchen and four in the bedroom.
how many chairs are there in both rooms together?
seven chairs.
if i move one from the bedroom back to the kitchen, what changes?
then there are four in the kitchen and three in the bedroom. the number together is still seven.
why did moving them not add a new chair?
because the same chairs changed places. you did not bring a chair from outside those two rooms.
now a friend brings one new chair and puts it in the kitchen.
then there are five in the kitchen and three in the bedroom, making eight together.
can you know whose all eight are?
no. you said your friend brought one, but not whose the other chairs are or whether the new chair is theirs.
my friend is a man. the old chairs are all mine and the new one is his.
you have seven chairs, and your friend has one.
what if i only ask how many are in the kitchen now?
five.
someone is giving me many examples, and i understand now. how can i say that without making them think i did not want help?
you could say: thank you. i understand it now, and i have enough examples to try it myself.
can i say i will ask again if i need more?
yes. that makes it clear you are ready to try, while leaving room for more help later.
write both parts together.
thank you. i understand it now and have enough examples to try myself. i will ask again if i need more help.
what if i do not understand yet but need a break?
then say that instead. i need a break before more examples is different from i understand now.
write a kind request for that break.
thank you for helping. i need a short break before we do more examples.
why not say i understand so they stop talking?
because that gives the wrong information about what you know. you can ask for a break without saying the question is already clear.
make that answer shorter.
you can ask for a break without saying you understand when you do not.
only give the sentence about a break again.
thank you for helping. i need a short break before we do more examples.
write a story about a child waiting for his father and learning why soon is not a specific time.

a child asked when his father would be ready to leave. his father said soon and went back to finishing a note. the child sat by the door, but after a while asked again. he did not know whether soon was about one minute or much longer. his father looked at what he still needed to do and said he needed five more minutes. now the child knew he had time to put his book away and get some water. when the five minutes were over, they checked whether they were both ready. a more specific answer had helped them use the waiting time.
why was soon hard for the child to use?
it did not give a specific number of minutes. he did not know how much he could do before leaving.
did five minutes mean the father could never be late?
no. five minutes gave a more specific plan. if the task took longer, he would need to tell the child.
what would help if it took longer?
the father could tell him about the change and give a new time if he knew one.
what could the child ask after hearing soon?
about how many minutes do you need before we leave?
make the father answer if he cannot know yet.
i am not sure yet. i will check what is left and tell you when i know.
finish with them leaving after another check.
his father put the note down and asked whether the book was away. the child said yes, and they went out together.
is would you read this sentence for me a request?
yes. it is a request asking someone to read the sentence for you.
can i say read this sentence without would you?
yes. read this sentence is a way to tell someone what to do. would you read this sentence is a question and often sounds less like an order.
make that explanation shorter.
read this sentence gives an order. would you read this sentence asks a question.
now add please.
would you please read this sentence for me?
can that sound like i am saying they must do it?
the words ask for help. the way you say them can still make the request feel calm or like an order.
give that explanation more simply.
the words are useful, and the way you say them can change how the person feels about the request.
now make it a request for only the first line.
would you please read only the first line for me?
why is only useful there?
it makes clear that you want the first line, rather than the whole page.
